content.jointProblem: Can Serbian morphology-aware retrieval combined with script canonicalization reduce LinguaBot’s support-search miss rate toward its below-5% target while allowing vocabulary updates without a full re-index? The first experiment would compare the current Elasticsearch baseline with normalization–morphology variants on held-out support queries, explicitly testing transfer from document retrieval to short queries, within-word script mixing, and newly introduced product terms.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly studied how Serbian morphological reduction interacts with script normalization, providing a basis for testing processing-order choices rather than treating these problems independently.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.

rationale.text: His work provides a concrete phoneme-based token canonicalization method for cross-script retrieval, with evaluation on annotated legal query–document pairs.

sources.quote: each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions
We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

rationale.text: He has investigated incremental mixed-script indexing, which is relevant to designing—but does not establish—a vocabulary-update mechanism that avoids full re-indexing.

sources.quote: Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja.

rationale.text: His production-load research offers candidate deterministic and selective neural-normalization configurations whose accuracy and latency can be tested within LinguaBot’s deployment constraints.

sources.quote: A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms.

rationale.text: He has experience with search-normalization modules integrated into company systems, although the evidence does not identify Elasticsearch compatibility.

sources.quote: Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe.

constraints.text: The prototype must address Serbian morphology and automatic script mixing, including within-word mixing, rather than only transliterating clean single-script text.

sources.quote: our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.
We need an approach that handles lemmatisation or indexing in a way that is accurate for Serbian, tolerates script mixing automatically

constraints.text: The design must fit the existing Elasticsearch search system and support new vocabulary without requiring a full re-index; continuing manual synonym-list maintenance is not an adequate solution.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

constraints.text: Evaluation should use the company’s labelled support data and linguist validation; access and suitable held-out relevance labels must be confirmed before relying on these resources.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.

constraints.text: Scope tooling and data work around the approximately EUR 8,000 budget and produce a testable prototype within six months.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: Keep the engagement a small, research-focused industrial project: the researcher reports capacity for only one smaller industrial contract or consulting engagement, and calendar availability remains unknown.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Transfer is unvalidated: results from legal, news, web and encyclopedia corpora do not establish performance on short bank/telecom support queries or within-word mixed-script typos. The first experiment must measure these cases separately.

Incrementally adding documents is not the same as changing morphological rules or canonical forms for already indexed terms. The no-full-re-index requirement may require a different query-time or versioned-index design.
Foreign names, abbreviations and alphanumeric product identifiers may be damaged by normalization. Published exception handling does not establish coverage of LinguaBot’s terminology.
Prior company pilots still required terminology-related module updates, so the proposed approach may not sufficiently reduce maintenance effort without a tested update workflow.
The below-5% miss-rate target is unvalidated; morphology and script fixes alone may leave misses caused by coverage gaps, ambiguity or ranking failures.

Researcher start date and committed hours, company engineering allocation, deployment hardware and latency limits are unknown. The stated tooling/data budget may not cover research labour or infrastructure.
Permission to use client support queries, privacy requirements and cross-client data-sharing boundaries are unknown and could restrict experimentation.
questions: Can the researcher confirm a start date and committed effort for a small six-month joint project, and which company engineers and linguists will be allocated?
Does the EUR 8,000 cover only tooling and data work, or also research fees, engineering effort and compute?
Can appropriately de-identified queries, response documents and relevance labels be shared under client agreements, and must experiments remain within company infrastructure?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth, and can the 12,000-query baseline be reproduced with client-separated and temporal held-out tests?
Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers and spaCy components are deployed, and are query-time expansion, custom plugins or additional index fields permitted?
Does 'without a full re-index' prohibit even a one-time migration, and must updates affect previously indexed content immediately?
What are the production latency, throughput, memory and hardware limits, and what precision or false-match regressions are unacceptable?

Can the first experiment include linguist-validated strata for inflection, cross-script queries, within-word mixing, foreign names and unseen quarterly terminology, plus a vocabulary-update test against existing indexed content?
